finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only a substring check for "example.io". An attacker can pass a URL such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io.attacker.com/ or http://attacker.com/#example.io. This makes the server request internal or arbitrary hosts, and the response body is returned to the attacker (full-read SSRF). Redirects are followed by default.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; it matches anywhere in the string (host, path, query, fragment, userinfo)
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, with no host, scheme or IP validation
the response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The substring check at line 32 is not a valid host allowlist, because the URL is never parsed and the host is never compared. There is no scheme restriction and no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking. There is no redirect restriction, since the default client follows redirects. It can be bypassed trivially.

verdict.guard_found: none (only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") substring check at main.go:32; the exact-host allowlist at main.go:20 applies only to the separate /cdn handler)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only does a substring check that passes for e.g. http://attacker.com/#example.io, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 returns the body to the caller.
